thread:
incident-bot: P0 — automated alert: surge in paging + KV working set growth on cluster redwood-prod-07. kvcache_evictions/sec up 5.6x, paging_iops 6x baseline, scheduler queue depth increased. Auto-paged to oncall at 2026-03-14T03:13:09Z (ts=1923456789).

alex (oncall): ack. I'm seeing short/text route 95p jump from ~70ms -> 1.8s. Dashboard shows large batches containing both small and huge requests.

kai: quick root hint: continuous-batching feature flag `coalesce_long_requests` set to true in yesterday's rollout; plus batch_window bumped to 45ms in batch-config#5. Canary traffic didn't include mixed tenants so missed this effect.

sophia: result: long requests hold model state and KV references for the whole batch duration -> hot prefixes churned -> cache thrash -> disk paging. Also noticed aborted-batch paths not releasing lock counters properly.

alex (oncall): mitigation priority = reduce customer impact ASAP. Options?

kai: immediate playbook: 1) flip `coalesce_long_requests=false` across prod-07 (dynamic) 2) set `batch_window_ms=10` 3) enable `short_request_preempt=true` to let small requests jump ahead. Also temporarily lower `max_concurrent_batches` from 64->24. I'll start flags.

deploy-bot: applying dynamic flags to redwood-prod-07. Progress: 2/8 hosts updated.

infra-bot: autoscaler: observed increased CPU due to paging; no node crashes.

cs-lead: CS signal: several customers reported timeouts on small-chat and embeddings; opening CS ticket CS-2307. We need a one-line holding message once we confirm mitigations.

sophia: additional quick step: set per-route token cap for heavy short routes: `/v1/short-chat` max_tokens=128 (dynamic).

alex (oncall): do it. Keep changes incremental to avoid cascade.

kai: flipping short-route caps now. deploy-bot: route config applied to 6/6 frontends.

deploy-bot: dynamic flags rolled to 5/8 hosts. Getting KV metrics now.

kai: early telemetry: kvcache miss rate moving from 66% -> 42% after 5 hosts. Paging_iops dropping but two hosts still show high eviction churn.

sophia: investigating code path — found bug where `kv_lock_count` isn't decremented when a coalesced batch is aborted due to overload. This leaves stale lock counts causing the eviction heuristics to escalate. I have a minimal hotfix to decrement on abort in the runtime: `runtime/kv/decr-on-abort`.

alex (oncall): what's risk of hotpatch?

sophia: small localized change, unit tested. Plan: canary on single node p07-04, observe 8-10m, then roll.

deploy-bot: starting canary deploy of `decr-on-abort` to p07-04.

pager: paging alert suppressed by oncall action. Sending update to rotation.

kai: canary logs look normal; no error spike. Proceeding with 3-node roll.

deploy-bot: patch at 3/8 hosts.

alex (oncall): monitoring kvcache_active_set and eviction counters. Keep CS in the loop.

cs-lead: drafting holding note: "We've detected transient latency and some errors caused by a batching change that allowed long prompts to monopolize batches, which caused cache thrashing and paging. We've applied emergency rate and batching changes and deployed a runtime fix. We're monitoring and will follow up with a postmortem."

kai: after patch rollout, eviction churn stopped on patched nodes. Global active KV working set trending down ~38% over 12m. Paging IOPS near baseline. Short-route 95p latency improving to ~140ms.

sophia: still seeing rare tail spikes on one host p07-02; digging logs — it had repeated large single-request prompts from an integration test tenant that exceeded per-request limit. I've throttled that tenant and applied a temporary route-specific max_tokens=256 on its route.

alex (oncall): good catch. Any lingering error rate increases?

kai: 5xxs have returned to baseline. No new timeouts reported in the last 20m.

deploy-bot: dynamic flags complete on 8/8 hosts; runtime patch rolled to 8/8 hosts.

incident-bot: incident state -> mitigated. P0 remains open for 90m to validate stability. Runbook link: runbooks/kv-cache-batching.md added.

alex (oncall): followups to track in postmortem: 1) Require perf-sig approval + mixed-workload canary for any change that increases batch_window_ms or enables coalescing long requests. 2) Implement scheduler tenant-aware fairness and preemption so many small requests can't be starved. 3) Add alert: KV active set growth >2x in 5m per AZ. 4) Harden aborted-batch path with unit/integration tests (simulate abort + lock counters). 5) Add CI mixed-workload test that runs at canary scale.

sophia: I'll own the runtime fix PR & tests. kai will lead canary gating changes. alex will coordinate postmortem and customer comms.

cs-lead: sending holding note to affected customers now. Will escalate if any reply.

alex (oncall): handing off monitoring to kai for the night watch. I'll write the incident timeline and send final customer ack after the stability window. Great response team. :thumbsup:

kai: taking watch. Monitoring KV metrics and batch-scheduler fairness dashboards. Created followup ticket INC-2026-07-batch-fairness assigned to kai/sophia.

incident-bot: log: rollback not required; mitigations = dynamic flag flips + per-route caps + runtime hotfix; followups created.

alex (oncall): end of thread for immediate mitigation.
